gen-silkscreen-gf-tuffy: Silkscreen spaces every letter apart so you can nearly feel the gaps, giving a lo-fi, retro heading. Tuffy takes over below in a plain sans, drawn like pencil that never presses harder.
gen-silkscreen-gf-urbanist: Urbanist writes with a single-width, rolling-ball line that never curls shut. Under Silkscreen's retro, spaced-out headings, that smooth trail is what makes the pair feel so deliberately modern.
gen-silkscreen-gf-varela: Approachable and modern in the body, Varela gives its t a crossbar and stem of one width and its c a wide mouth. Silkscreen up top stays lo-fi.
gen-silkscreen-gf-varela-round: Varela Round reads clean and modern, with counters framed by same-width strokes and wide-mouthed rounds in the lowercase. Silkscreen's retro spacing makes it feel playful beside it.
gen-silkscreen-gf-varta: Chunky retro meets quiet modern. Silkscreen's diagonals are as thick as its uprights, which gives it punch, while Varta, a plain sans, lets its big open eyes on e and a do the reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-vazirmatn: Vazirmatn keeps its s wide open and never tightens it. Silkscreen is best at monoline, lo-fi display lettering, while the sans below handles approachable, modern text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-wix-madefor-display: Silkscreen draws everything in a unit-width stroke, retro and spaced out. Wix Madefor Display follows in sans-serif with gently flared curve ends that stay apart, and a modest size step between them would suit.
gen-silkscreen-gf-wix-madefor-text: Professional in manner, Wix Madefor Text offers easy-to-read open terminals. Its quiet sans clarity set against Silkscreen's constant-line, retro lettering is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ysabeau: Ysabeau brings sweeping curves that never close up, giving the body a professional but approachable warmth. And Silkscreen's spaced-out, lo-fi letters sit above it like pixel signage over a friendly sans.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ysabeau-infant: Blocky retro charm up top, soft and contemporary below: Silkscreen builds uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, while Ysabeau Infant flicks its terminals outward like tongs. One gets attention, the other keeps it.
